root_cause.text: The `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` function lacks validation to ensure that the per-CPU CID is actually CPU-owned (having the `ONCPU` bit set) before dropping it, which causes an out-of-bounds bit clearing operation when the `TRANSIT` bit is set instead.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` in `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()`, and the commit message states that `sched_mm_cid_exit()` invokes `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` which "clears the not set ONCPU bit and then invokes clear_bit() with an insanely large bit number because TRANSIT is set (bit 29)."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard check to ensure a CID is active on the CPU before attempting to drop it.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` around the CID clearing and dropping logic in `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu`.
intent_record.how: Prevents modifying the per-CPU CID and calling `mm_drop_cid` if the CID is not currently marked as active on the CPU, avoiding redundant or incorrect state updates.

relevance_review.reason: The group only updates a comment to clarify behavior and does not modify any code logic or address the missing validation in mm_drop_cid_on_cpu().

The group's core intent is to add a guard check to ensure a CID is active on the CPU before dropping it, which directly addresses the vulnerability root cause where mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() lacked validation to ensure the CID was CPU-owned before dropping it.

candidates.rationale: This statement converts the per-CPU CID to a regular CID by clearing the ONCPU bit without first validating if the CID is actually CPU-owned (i.e., has the ONCPU bit set). If the TRANSIT bit is set instead, this results in an invalid CID value.
This statement attempts to drop the CID using the unvalidated CID value, which causes an out-of-bounds bit clearing operation in the CID bitmap when the TRANSIT bit is set instead of the ONCPU bit.
